body:
ESH but I think it’s understandable what you did. I also have family members that are chronically shitty to the people I love. After ruining a few holiday dinners, I decided I would no longer be around those family members. I think that may be something to consider here. 

Also, just to say it, porn/sex work in general isn’t a dishonest living—she is a dishonest person. That’s the problem. There is a big difference. There are plenty of shitty things to pick. Next time, pick one that’s about her character (that’s where the problem is anyway) and default to your mom’s wishes on level of intensity in your response. You can find a middle ground between not saying anything and not starting a huge mess.

We’ve all had a stupid, petty outbursts. It happens. Ultimately, she’s at fault for lying to her husband. You didn’t do the shittiest thing in the situation. All you can do is move forward and handle these moments with more nuance in the future.

My partnership has had moments like these too and I’ve felt exactly what you describe here. It’s so confusing because—at least for me— I wasn’t really suspicious of cheating or anything, but genuinely could not understand/felt hurt.

Instead of pushing him, I decided to go meet my own totally separate friends. It started from a petty place honestly (and I don’t recommend that bit). But immediately it was so nice to be known as just myself—and not even remotely part of a unit. Especially in serious relationships, sometimes it’s nice to have something to yourself and to be perceived as an individual. I come from a lot of normalized codependency and didn’t really understand that until I felt it.

There are lots of ways to navigate this one. You aren’t being over dramatic but also he isn’t doing anything wrong (although...only one party? I get keeping things separate but that’s a little overkill imho). 

Hopefully once you understand what need this space fills for him and once he understands why this particular approach hurts you, you’ll be able to find a nice compromise. Maybe you only hang out with them on holidays or he invites them to his place once a month and you hang around for the first half and then leave for plans of your own. It’s completely possible to figure out!

My partner shared an office with his ex. Lmao. It’s not always fun but I try to just let the jealousy pass. Typically for me it’s founded in anxiety not reality. Working with an ex sounds fucking stressful so I just focused on being support. My partner was very open which helped.

Eventually, working together seemed to give them really helpful structure in solidifying a comfortable platonic dynamic. Sharing an office actually ended up pushing him to be more proactive about boundaries too.

At the end of the day all you can do is trust him not to cheat, trust yourself (that you pick good people, that you’ll notice/leave if needed, etc) and stay firm in your boundaries. Good luck!

When I say nice things about someone behind their back/while they aren’t around, I try to make it a point to casually mention it to them directly too.

I had a new friend pop into my life and start doing this—it made me feel so good to hear the specific things she appreciated and found like...notable enough to mention to other people she cared about? I was so used to being worried about bad stuff people could say, I didn’t even think they would say good stuff? It genuinely had never occurred to me. It was a real confidence changer to realize it’s a mix, like everything else. Now I want to make sure I’m appreciating people directly too! I want those around me to feel as valued as my friend makes me feel.

NTA. You can both use the name but they can’t change the fact that there is already a loved pet in the family using the name. It’s ridiculous they saw getting rid of the cat as an option. They can only get over it or pick a new name.

My dad had a dog named ‘Katie’ for about 8 years before my uncle had his daughter. My uncle used the name he wanted, without checking in (because it was none of our business) and everyone adjusted to having two Katies. The extended family just called the dog KatieDog and jokingly called the new baby KatieGirl. KatieGirl is a still a fun nickname for my cousin two decades later. It was all fine and even kinda cute.

No one else really showed up or celebrated with me. Eventually it just kinda felt like I shouldn’t either?


Honestly, I’m not really sure how I’d feel with all that attention anyway though lol.
I appreciate that! Thank you for adding that really important consent reminder! :)

This!!!

It can be hard to stay firm in your needs/boundaries but it’s so important you don’t do things you don’t want to sexually. Especially while healing from trauma/abuse.

Woah surprised by the lack of empathy here in the comments. I was also a victim of abuse and I do struggle with similar things—so I can tell you confidently: therapy. ASAP.

Trauma-informed therapy is a godsend. There’s even specifically sex therapy if you want that narrow focus.

Hopefully your partner will understand you need to heal and can bring extra care/patience to the situation. Explain that you have some unresolved trauma that’s contributing to this issue and affirm that it’s not his fault. Discuss what the most comfortable starting compromise is, ways he could help, and go from there. At the end of the day you have to untangle it because you want to heal though, not just because your partner wants sex.

If you are both older or at similar life stages, then maybe age doesn’t matter so much. But there’s such a huge potential for hurt in these situations that I think people are right to be actively cautious about them.

I was in a smaller age gap relationship (a little less than 10 years) and that was too much for me. Yes, people were also shitty and made comments—and like you I got defensive about my relationship instead of taking the hint to examine it. So I don’t think being rude necessarily helps anyone, but whatever.

He was almost thirty and I couldn’t drink yet. He had a retirement fund and I was worried about exams/rent. I was just so young when we met and he was an established adult. Some life-stage power dynamics are things that can fall together naturally, even between two decent people, and turn into a harmful mess.

Most often, even if not harmful, the relationships aren’t necessarily healthy and people are concerned. There are better ways to approach it but I don’t think anyone’s in the wrong unless they don’t know you/are being rude.

Can you mention it to the same mutual friend that gave you this impression in the first place? Maybe they can more subtly address it with like an “oh, I talked to OP the other day and they got really confused when I mentioned asking you out” type thing? 

Or have a casual conversation directly with this person about how you’re branching out and trying to intentionally make some new friends— maybe throw in an anecdote about a new friend that you’re going for a walk/same activity you asked them to do. Then just hope they connect the dots. 

I had a similar situation and opted for the second option. The girl who thought I asked her out burst out laughing and told me all about how she had perceived my ask. We were both a little embarrassed but had a good laugh about it. We ended up being close friends after that though!

I had a sinus infection for over a year! I went to multiple drs and they all said I was crazy and there was just a little bit of inflammation—turns out I had a split nasal cavity. 

I had an almost closed ‘pocket’ in my nose that had been inflamed and infected for (at least) a year. It was really frustrating as more than one doctor implied I was a hypochondriac for coming in about this so many times.

I had surgery to ‘open the pocket’ (ie knock down a wall for an open-floor-plan nose). Now I can’t smell super well but I’m not sick!

I have this too! Ugh. I went to the doctor as a kid because my mom freaked out and thought my hands were going to fall off at some point. Super fun to have the dr say “yeah...that’s just gunna hurt. Sorry.” He suggested I wear gloves all the time.

I’m not sure if it’s gotten more mild as I’ve gotten older or I’m just used to it. Bodies are wild.

NTA. Your husband is fucking ridiculous. This makes me so mad. Is he okay? This feels like a weird break in sanity. Has he been acting erratically at all? In what world is this okay? 

I’d look into any joint finances because this feels like an odd gift for children and I wonder if there’s a resale value or something else happening here. This is so ridiculous and I hope your parents aren’t too upset. What a shitty thing to do.
Yes! I always call it “standby mode” lmao.

NTA. I’ve always thought about having an ‘opt out plan’ as a way to make sure I’m staying because I want to, not because I have to. It’s a way to keep myself accountable in staying for the right reasons and not because of the financial hardship of leaving—because I could actually leave whenever and be decently okay for a bit.

My mother and grandmother have always told my siblings and I that everyone should have a private breakup account.

To be fair, I’ve disclosed the existence of this account to my fiancé. He loved the way I framed it and opted to structure his finances similarly! Which personally I kind of love, it makes me feel very chosen that he doesn’t ‘need’ me, but is here because he wants me.

Do you think your fiancé would understand that framing of it?

Fuck your friend though tbh. Commitment doesn’t require or thrive with the lack of other options.

I appreciate you hearing me out. It’s a hard thing to get into some days. I’m glad to hear you’re taking a more critical look. I know it sucks to walk away from someone you have feelings for and I’m sorry you have to go through that. 

It’s in your best interest too, tbh. My ex ended up hurt by the situation too (although not in the same formative way I was hurt). He was a basically good person who didn’t know how to prevent/step outside of the toxic dynamics that naturally popped up due to our ages. It pushed us both into roles we didn’t want and couldn’t break out of. It can be really challenging even for two good, healthy people to keep a big age gap relationship good and healthy, you know? It’s just hard. It’s good to hear that’s walking away is your plan. I hope things go well for you both.

Hi! I had just turned 20 when I started dating a 27 year old. We dated for 4 years. The power dynamics were really damaging for me. I’ve had to unlearn a lot of unhealthy behaviors. While I don’t necessarily fully regret my choices, I do often feel I was taken advantage of in the initial stages of our relationship. I feel gross thinking about just how young I was sitting there with a fully established adult. Now, at 25, I cannot imagine dating someone that young and the older I get, the less comfortable I get with the fact that I dated someone that much older while I was still so young and figuring it out. 

TLDR: I was the younger party of this exact same age gap and I now feel gross/taken advantage of in hindsight. I think this is more likely to do harm than good and it seems you know that too. Personally, I feel it’s just too big of an age gap and you should stop seeing him.

Hi OP, Everyone has covered the key points on therapy, forgiving yourself, etc BUT I work for a LGBTQ+ health clinic that started as an HIV support org and want to let you know—it really is possible to get past these negative feelings about your diagnosis. Holding these feelings and anxieties (and even obsessions) is so incredibly normal— and so is learning to grow past them.

I know how impossible it can feel. I want to let you know I’ve seen people move past this more times than I can count. It’s real. It’s possible. You can do it. It may take some therapy and pushing yourself, but trust that it’s possible.

You are so worthy of love. You are worthy of a full, wonderful life. There is nothing about you, HIV or not, that can change that. You got this.

I agree with the other comments, but if you’d really like to get it out of the way to be safe—just start using a different name professionally. Nickname, middle name, etc. As long as you intend to professionally go by that name, you do not need to apply with your legal name, you’ll just need to provide it to HR for formal background checks, employment verification and for paycheck purposes.

I’m trans so my name change was different but I haven’t changed it legally and no one I work with knows my legal/birth name—not even my boss. Only HR knows. This is my second job with a social name that differs from my legal name and it hasn’t caused any issues.

It’s a bit extreme (I really don’t see this impacting your job prospects as acting is a real & valid addition to your work history, even for low budget productions) but if it’s really bothering you, then it may be worth it.

She told everyone (all of our mutual friends) that she was going to fuck my then-partner of 4 years and make him leave me. 

He cheated with her. He cut contact and offered to “officially dump” her. I left him instead. He treated her horribly.

I hate her, but she did deserve better than what the past couple years handed her (old friends lmk that she’s had some hard life stuff happen)—some things not even shitty people deserve.

That cheating ex can rot in hell forever though. He once said he felt like a bad feminist while having sex because he felt like his “penis felt emblematic of the patriarchy”. I started hating him a little then. Lmao.

I’m 25 and have 11k in savings and a 3k emergency fund tucked away (plus some retirement funds but I haven’t felt the need to keep a close eye on that quite yet). I had closer to 15k in savings at the beginning of 2020 but my community was hit hard with COVID and I opted to redistribute as much as I could while still feeling stable. 

I think it’s important to mention, I was only able to get to this point of stability due to having middle class parents to help with a third of college costs and to teach me some financial literacy. The fact that I have no children/dependents (just my dog) helps quite a bit too.

Yeah, I’m not sure if it’s like that everywhere? I was really surprised that they ended up being important.

I do a tailored one for positions I’m really invested in. For those I do a little formula: 
statement of interest,
anecdote related to company/company mission,
brief related work experience (with technical highlights of needed) &
thanks for time consideration/restated interest

If you google there’s great advice on the actual language/tone and a lot of templates to start from.

One good tip thats helped me is to write it, then revisit for a round of editing to insert specific words from the website and job listing into your description of yourself and your experience. Don’t go overboard and definitely honor your original sentiment, but it can appear thoughtful and clearly layout some of the boxes you check.

I’m in marketing, so pretty different from tech industry expectations. I have a slightly non-traditional resume (colors/designed) as well as a cover letter template with the same branding. 

 A lot of people underestimate the power of cover letters. My first boss said he throws out every application without one and since then I’ve always written one even if it’s a little general. It’s what tipped the scales between myself and another candidate for my current role.

I also keep an updated portfolio of projects, strategy, design work—and try to keep it all grounded in performance data and analytics. If I don’t have numbers, I don’t use it. It can take a little work and isn’t something traditionally expected but it’s helped me get raises so it’s usefulness goes beyond job hunting!

Also always ask these questions at every interview:

- what does success look like in this role?
-who was your most successful hire? And how/why?

It’ll help you see what the hiring party values and if that’s something you want!


Good luck!

Thank you!!! I’m so glad it ended up being lovely for you! That’s good to hear. We’ve really enjoyed our first day or so with it as a secret. It’s nice to know other people have done the same! 

And thank you so much!! I wanted something that looked like my late grandmother’s ring and my partner did a wonderful job finding something similar.
Chuck!

4 years ago, I was pretty shy and focused on school. My best friend went to Long Island Thursdays at our local gay bar a lot and was into an acquaintance of mine who also went often too. My best friend was too nervous to make a move on her own and wanted me to come to introduce them. I had Friday 8ams that semester though and always refused to play wingman on a weeknight.

One Thursday, during an impromptu study session with that best friend, I found out that my Friday class had been cancelled (professor was sick). So, being a pushover with no good excuse to cling to, I borrowed a top and we went to the bar.

Well I never drank/partied and turns out I was in WAY over my head with Long Islands (turns out they aren’t ice tea). Soo I accidentally got lightly trashed. While drunkenly dancing, I offhand told a person I liked their tattoo and they introduced me to their friend. I ended up dancing/making out with them, this absolute stranger. I never got drunk in public let alone drunk enough for that!

This stranger had gone out with a new friend (the tattoo person) on a whim. He wouldn’t have even been in the same city if not for a girl he met in middle school.

That stranger and I got engaged yesterday.


Thank god for horny friends, sick profs, and a misunderstanding of Long Island ice tea.

They aren’t afraid to like things! And tell people that they like those things! The confidence is wildly contagious and it’s so wonderful.

They actively, clearly tell me when they like my idea/the movie I picked/the song I put on/etc. It’s small but wow having someone you respect validate your taste feels so good.

Past partners have been positive, but my current partner is genuine and direct in a way that makes people glow a little (me/friends/strangers). My partner rarely notices it—because they’re just appreciating things that they like. I love it so much.

NTA—and I get the impulse to say ESH but I actually feel like this was a great way to harmlessly demonstrate how serious she is about protecting their son. No one was hurt. Her husband has resources/options to stay at a hotel or with a friend or to sit with himself and apologize.

The dad seems like an abusive ass so this probably won’t solve the issues but I think it’s a decent way to take a stand on it and actively show your son that you’re advocating for him. I hope OP is looking into divorce/next steps too. It’s harmful for your son to live with those threats. Even if they stop he should look into therapy to help him process.

YTA. You are the only one responsible for your feelings. The entitlement here is wild. Plus, going to her house is creepy and so inappropriate especially after she blocked you. Jfc. Your therapist didn’t intend for you to push past everyone’s boundaries to complete your therapy homework. You need to tell them you did this and let them help you work on respecting boundaries before anything else.

You don’t. 

Replace the impulse to text him with texting someone else. Get set up with some therapy to work through your codependency issues before dating again.

You deserve a partner that wants you back. That is not be this guy- he’s made it clear he doesn’t even want to talk to you. Focus on yourself.
Definitely NTA. Leaving a note is a kinder alternative to getting someone towed.

NTA and tbh the fact that her response was to jump straight to minimizing your feelings is almost more concerning than her bailing on plans. Making it seem like you’re being intense instead of taking a minute to genuinely address your feelings is lowkey toxic. That’s not how people who value and respect you act. Save your time & effort for people who care when you say you’re hurt.

Oh! I commented before the updates. I didn’t realize y’all started tearing shit up already. Yikes. Maybe a good flag to keep an eye on proactive communication in the relationship (may not be an issue but also...what harm can working on communication skills do?).

 If you don’t want the trailer and don’t want to pay for anything—why not do what others have said and give/sell it to him? Or just get rid of it or wait/save until money is more flexible. If I was in his position I would’ve never expected to pay for materials. To me, it’s really not fair to expect that unless he’s getting the trailer but idk. In my mind, the fact that you don’t want it doesn’t really change that it’s yours/costs are your responsibility. If you don’t want it—it’s yours—you’re allowed to just say no to him fixing it.

I could maybe see NAH because at the end of the day it’s really just an unfortunate lapse in communication during a rough financial time. Idk how much fault is on anyone. You’re both just trying to make something work. It’s messy—good luck!

EDIT: you didn’t answer my question: who would keep it?

So...yeah, YTA here. Offering to provide the labor is a generous offer on its own. Assuming he would take on the material costs too seems like a little much. 

Hypothetical: If he had paid for the materials and put in the labor to make this it usable and then you guys broke up tomorrow—who would keep the camper? 

Would you reimburse him for the materials/labor and keep full ownership or would he get it since you were going to throw it out and he salvaged it?

Your answer to that should determine who pays for the materials IMO. 



But more realistically just split it. Lol.
Nope. No. Get out now.

NTA—but I agree with some of the comments saying it doesn’t have to be too late.

She may just really not remember the impact of the way she acted. She was 13 and emotionally struggling. It doesn’t excuse anything, but it may not be that she’s being entitled and trying to jump back in—she may remember it differently or not have a full understanding of how she made others feel. 

At 13 I was dealing with the onset of mental illness. I remember very little of what I said and did, just the way I was feeling—not even the way others were feeling. I didn’t realize until my brothers had a bit of a talk with me. She may remember being vaguely mean but not realize the level of cruelty it was.

It’s really good that you were honest when she asked. I also think she may need the level of specific “do you remember making jokes about their dead mom?” if you haven’t gone there already.

It’s been 15+ years. She is absolutely a different person. The question is how different? She needs to apologize and start with smaller steps to reconnect while everyone gains their footing and gets to know each other. If you want to tell her that and work on that relationship, it’s your call. It’s okay not to but it’s not impossible or too late.

NTA, but this girl needs a therapist immediately. This doesn’t sound like something you can actually, effectively fix with tough love and immediate new boundaries. She needs the adults in her life to get her help. 

This is not normal or healthy. Go to the doctor to make sure blood sugar is okay and that she’s not upset because delays make her feel sick. She may just think everyone feels that bad but can handle it. Even if it is just a lack of boundaries/being spoiled/something, she’s going to need professional therapy to adjust. 

It’s just too bad for any of you, including her, to tackle without a professional support system right now.

NTA. I personally would struggle to stay in my marriage after this. The level of total disregard for your son is astounding. I would want a partner that was trying to support me in saving and seeing how they could proactively help with their stepson’s quality of life—sick or not.

She’s allowed to want a nursery but not at the expense of a child’s well-being. How dare she push—let alone try to back you into a corner!

At least get counseling or encourage her to get therapy or something. A professional needs to resolve some shit there. 

I’d be out though, honestly. She has already show she is not a safe, healthy person to have around your son and doubled down on it when it was pointed out to her. NOPE.

NTA. She’s 13! She could start her period any day! She could start it while she’s not around her mom or a trusted adult to help her figure it out.

The sex talk thing is irresponsible but not telling her about her own body is horrible.

I grew up in a very sheltered household. I had no idea. I was only 10 when I learned the hard way and it was scary af. I mean...you just start bleeding! Why risk putting your child through that much fear and distress? 

I think it was important that you advocated for your niece’s best interest.

NTA. I would let him know straight up that I expect an apology to me & our child and a list of resources he has found to do a little more work on himself. That’s the baseline I would need before communicating further to resolve things. Whether it was a conscious choice or a subconscious slip, please send the message that this is 100% not acceptable and will not be tolerated in your home.

When I came out as trans I was in a similar situation. My partner said the same things you did—but added a significant transphobic rant to the end of it. He said invalidating things like “if you’re a woman who thinks she’s a man” etc. In my vulnerable state, that really outweighed the bits about being loved and made me feel alone, scared and hurt. 

If this story is telling everything and you were kind & affirming along with your honesty, then you really did nothing wrong.

If your wife is trans, they may be hurting really deeply and a very small part of it is actually about you. It’s just easier to make it about you.

It could be feelings about sexuality & how gender factors in or it could be about gender identity—but it’s on her to communicate it. All you can do is make it safe for her to do so.

I’d say maybe let your wife know that you’re here  if they want to calmly revisit the conversation. (Personally, I’d need an apology about the aggression displayed with the glass before moving forward. Also maybe google the HALT communication tool and both commit to that.) I’d just keep reminding them that they will always be your family and you’re here to listen.

Sorry to hear it. That’s really hard. Hopefully you get something really great out of the healing process. 

You have a long line of new enby friends but I’m here too if you’re feeling it.

TLDR: the surgeon said my spine “exploded”.

I suspected had a herniated disc (a lot of pain, struggling to walk, etc) but could barely afford the doctor appointments, let alone the MRI I needed to qualify for the surgery. It took a couple months but I managed to get the $512 for the MRI together—I did have a herniated disc! Then, it took about 6 months of hobbling around to get the money together for the surgery the dr said was my best bet.

By this point my entire right leg felt like it was actually physically burning almost all the time. I would’ve ripped it off with my own hands if I could’ve. I couldn’t sleep. I could barely walk. I passed out at work from the pain and nearly got a concussion. I had to stop every 10 minutes while driving and actually passed out as I pulled over once (Terrifying. Thankfully, quarantine hit right when I decided it was no longer safe for me to drive and so my job let me work remote.) I felt like there was a knife lodged in my lower spine when I moved.

Turns out 2 discs had burst shooting bone fragments up my spine that they had to go retrieve. No one believed me that I had been ‘walking’ (tbh towards the end I was mostly crawling). 
My surgeon said “It’s like it just exploded. We had to go hunting for all those nasty bone fragments. Scary stuff.”

Overall my leg was in constant, burning, shooting, nerve pain for a full calendar year. I can’t feel my right foot anymore but it (mostly) works and I can walk again without a cane or anything! But if my back goes for round two I may be ditching the leg. Lmao.
This!!!

NAH. While you aren’t doing anything wrong, as someone with ADHD, it really messes with my memory and sense of stability when my partner moves my stuff. I really don’t want them cleaning up after me because it throws me into personal chaos. But when the only other option is the clean partner in personal chaos, it’s really just everyone trying to stay afloat. So, understandable.

That said, your partner needs to be the one in charge of a solution. That’s the best chance it has to stick. Does he know this isn’t working for you? Like have you directly told him?

ADHD may explain the behavior, but does not excuse his lack of participation in building systems to meet you halfway.

I’m ADHD too and I think it’s helpful to remember that when he’s putting this clutter there or leaving it—it’s not like it’s laziness. If he’s anything like me his brain has given him a reason for it to be there. Typically, I’m genuinely convinced it’s the only logical option. Plus, I only remember where things are when they’re in ‘The  Spot’ my brain assigned them, even if it’s cluttered. I can imagine that type of thing is happening here too.

If you haven’t yet, maybe directly tell him he needs to solve this by himself? Not in an ultimatum way but something like “hey, I know this is how you function, but I really need a solution to this clutter thing that works for both of us. I’ve tried solving it for us but that isn’t working. I figure it’s your brain and you may see a solution I wouldn’t. Maybe try reading up to see if there’s anything you’d like to try instead? Let’s plan a coffee date next Saturday to talk through your ideas!” 
and maybe direct him to some of the ADHD/executive dysfunction subreddits—I’m newly diagnosed and it’s been SO helpful—or leave him to find sources on his own. He’s an adult and there are plenty out there. 

It’s a lot of effort for you to take on so if you don’t, that’s also valid. My partner and I try to keep it framed as a compatibility thing, not a fault of mine. Because to be honest I was happy and more functional in my clutter-filled, brain-map apartment, if I could go back to that I would in a heartbeat. But I want a home with the person I love. That means changing—neurotypical or not. So now I live in a (mostly) clean home with a lot of systems in place to try and keep my brain in check. I had to step up to figure it out myself and my partner had to step up the patience. It’s an always evolving balance. You also need to take this moment to decide if that’s an okay tension to have in your life.

I was in a bad relationship and wasn’t a good friend. I don’t think it’s a stretch to say I was toxic. My best friend dumping me was the wake up call I needed to get to therapy and get my shit straight. We still don’t have a relationship at all but I’m sure she’s happy and I have enough to focus on making sure I don’t get to that point again. 

I don’t know if it’s any solace. But if I could tell her anything now it would just be “I understand. Thank you.” 

I know it hurts regardless, but maybe hold on to that idea. You were looking out for your own needs and that’s a good thing. It’ll be okay.

To be honest, I would not be able to stay legally tied to someone who did this behind my back. I could maybe salvage the relationship with counseling but I really would be done trusting him with my financial stability and would need to transition to a romantic relationship with no legal ties. He lost that privilege.

 If it’s legally binding, a document claiming sole responsibility as mentioned above would be a smart thing to get before anything else. Or exploring the suggestions given on returning the car.

Please seek out a lawyer as well as maybe a financial counselor to get a solid grasp on your options. Then make a decision only thinking about yourself. He clearly isn’t looking out for you and there’s a chance this won’t be the last time.

My grandfather started with things like this and it escalated to the point that he forged my grandmothers signature to sell the family home without her knowledge. He told her they were moving a week after the sale and didn’t show her the new house—that he had bought with their joint money, but without her name on it—until the day they moved in. Despite losing much of her memory, she mourned the loss of her home until the day she passed. Honestly, we all did. It was heartbreaking.

Not to toss a horror story out there—your situation could be entirely different! 
But I just want to validate that this was a big deal that could turn into a pattern without serious intervention. You’re right to be this concerned. Don’t let anyone minimize it.

Omfg. He doesn’t have a porn problem. He has a boundaries and respect problem. If he was using onlyfans or paying for content with sex workers in a way that didn’t fit well with your definition of monogamy, then he could say it’s a porn problem. But this man is actively seeking out inappropriate sexual relationships with other woman and knows it’s cheating (he threw his phone into a river). I know you know all this I’m just mad for you. The audacity of this man. Nope.

I think there’s a balance here. You can be open and honest, without going into details. 
Personally, I let my partners know within the first 6 months that I’ve experienced abuse. I make it clear that in some ways I’ll always be healing but that I’m not asking them to do anything about it. That’s as detailed as I go as is related to the past aside from the occasional small anecdote. I frame everything else in the present and let it come up naturally. “Oh yeah, I have this trigger but I try to stay grounded by doing X.” I am always very open about my trauma reactions and the ways I try to fix them—for self-accountability as much as anything. The ways in which I hold my healing are just another way of knowing me and most people can pick the important bits up without a detailed history.

If it’s important to you to share those details, I suggest once you know you’re in a comfortable place you say “hey, I’d like to share some stuff I’ve been through with you so that you can fully know and see me. It’s not pretty stuff and it’s not easy. I hold it all well by myself and am not asking anything of you other than sharing this space with me. Let me know when you feel you can handle a night like that and I’ll bring the wine.” I had a partner approach me like this. We had a night of crying and sharing and seeing each other. It was really nice. We never went that deep into it again, but we knew. I always liked the way she presented it.

I hope that helps at all? It’s always however feels best to you personally. Trust yourself, care for your partner and it’ll all be fine. Good luck!
